feedback.summary: You produced a balanced report with a clear ethical stance to not ship. Your INTRODUCTION and stakeholder analysis are strong, and your healthcare argument is compelling. To improve, correct key factual errors, add missing report elements and visuals, and extend decision guidance to all stakeholders with stronger evidence.
next_steps: Correct your 1% of 5,000 calculation to 50 in DISCUSSION: To Ship or Not to Ship and fix the Volkswagen description in The Most Ethical Path to diesel emissions cheating.
Add the missing abstract and at least one visual element like a stakeholder map or risk table, fix DICUSSION spelling, and complete your References entries.
Extend your RECOMMENDATION and conclusion to give tailored decision guidance for the chip supplier, health department and customers, not just Rachel and her company.

criteria.C1: You did well in INTRODUCTION identifying quality vs business success, safety and professional responsibility and listing stakeholders. To hold Excellent, keep linking each issue explicitly to engineering design and organisational context.
criteria.C2: You did well in DISCUSSION: To Ship or Not to Ship presenting three for and multiple against arguments leading to not ship. For Excellent you need significant depth plus decision recommendations tailored for several different stakeholders.
criteria.C3: Your for/against then synthesis in The Most Ethical Path and CONCLUSION logically supports not ship. For Excellent you need systematic coverage of ethical issues for all stakeholders including supplier and health department.
criteria.C4: You used NHS, VW and ethics code sources well in The Most Ethical Path. For Very good you need adequate references with accurate qualitative and quantitative evidence and stronger balance.
criteria.C5: Your writing is mostly fluent but you have no abstract or visuals and incomplete references. For Good you need appropriate sections, competent visuals, and few relevant well-structured references.
